preview.subject: HANGS Construction Services Q3 2026 Seattle business tax return
preview.body:
Hello,

Attached are the Q3 2026 billing register by city and the Q3 general ledger for HANGS Construction Services LLC. The Seattle account details, the job list, the Q1 and Q2 Seattle returns, the state returns for July to September and the invoice for change order 6 on Pier 9 Tech Center are in the shared folder.

We missed the October 31 due date for the Q3 Seattle return while I was out. Please prepare it now as a draft for review; we will file and pay it ourselves in FileLocal. It is separate from the state returns we file in My DOR.

Duwamish Gateway sits across the Seattle and Tukwila line. Our project manager thinks about 60% of the work was on the Seattle parcel, but we do not have a survey split or a cost split yet, so everything was coded to Seattle.

We wrote off the Fremont Bakehouse balance (invoice HGC-25-0917) on September 30. That invoice was reported as Seattle revenue on our Q4 2025 Seattle return.

Dana Whitfield
Controller, HANGS Construction Services

messages.subject: HANGS Construction Services Q3 2026 Seattle business tax return
messages.body:
Hello,

Attached are the Q3 2026 billing register by city and the Q3 general ledger for HANGS Construction Services LLC. The Seattle account details, the job list, the Q1 and Q2 Seattle returns, the state returns for July to September and the invoice for change order 6 on Pier 9 Tech Center are in the shared folder.

We missed the October 31 due date for the Q3 Seattle return while I was out. Please prepare it now as a draft for review; we will file and pay it ourselves in FileLocal. It is separate from the state returns we file in My DOR.

Duwamish Gateway sits across the Seattle and Tukwila line. Our project manager thinks about 60% of the work was on the Seattle parcel, but we do not have a survey split or a cost split yet, so everything was coded to Seattle.

We wrote off the Fremont Bakehouse balance (invoice HGC-25-0917) on September 30. That invoice was reported as Seattle revenue on our Q4 2025 Seattle return.

Dana Whitfield
Controller, HANGS Construction Services

sources.title: Service Income Apportionment
sources.issuer: City of Seattle, Office of City Finance

passages.q: How is a job that straddles the Seattle city line divided?
passages.a: Businesses that report revenue under the classification of "Service and Other Business Activities" on their City of Seattle business tax return will calculate apportionment of this revenue. ... If your business does not have income to report under the classification of "Service and Other Business Activities," you will not calculate apportionment.

sources.title: City Finance: Business Taxes
sources.issuer: City of Seattle, Office of City Finance

passages.q: Is the Seattle return part of the state excise return?
passages.a: The Seattle business license tax is not the same as the Washington State B&O tax. You must file your Seattle taxes separately from your state taxes.

passages.q: When was the Q3 2026 return due, and what does filing it late cost?
passages.a: 3rd quarter ends Sept. 30 Oct. 31 ... 1st month after the due date 9% of tax owed 2nd month after the due date 19% of tax owed 3rd month after the due date or anytime after 29% of tax owed

sources.title: Deductions from the Business License Tax
sources.issuer: City of Seattle, Office of City Finance

passages.q: Are the Bellevue and Tacoma jobs taxed by Seattle?
passages.a: When you file, include the deduction amount in your gross amount. ... Taxed by other cities You can deduct revenue from the sale of tangible goods or retail services when you deliver them to another part of Washington, outside Seattle. Identify each city you deliver to. Use the Taxed by Other Cities deduction if the delivery location imposes a local gross receipts tax (B&O tax).

passages.q: Can the Fremont Bakehouse write-off be deducted?
passages.a: Bad debts and uncollected revenue You can deduct money that you previously reported as taxable revenue but were later unable to collect.

passages.q: May subcontractor costs, materials or retainage be taken out of gross?
passages.a: The costs of doing business cannot be deducted from your gross revenue amount. ... Only deductions specifically defined in the Seattle Municipal Code are allowed. ... Sales tax in gross Use this deduction to back out sales, admission or excise tax revenue that you included in the gross amount.

sources.title: Director's Rule 5-013, Business License Tax Threshold and Standard Deduction
sources.issuer: City of Seattle, Office of City Finance

passages.q: How much standard deduction is left for the Q3 return?
passages.a: Taxpayers filing business license tax returns on a quarterly installment basis shall apply the entire $2 million standard deduction toward taxable amounts commencing with the earliest quarter in the calendar year that the taxpayer has taxable revenue until the $2 million standard deduction amount is reached ... A taxpayer may not carry forward to a subsequent tax year amounts of their $2 million standard deduction that they were unable to apply during the current tax year.

sources.title: Tax Rates and Classifications
sources.issuer: City of Seattle, Office of City Finance

passages.q: What city B&O rates apply in 2026?
passages.a: Tax Classifications & Rates 2026-2032 ... Wholesaling .00342 Retail Sales & Retail Services .00342 Service & Other Business Activities .00658

passages.q: Which classification do the prime contracts and the subcontract go under?
passages.a: Report revenue under Retail Services if you perform services on tangible products. ... Examples of retail services: Repair or installation of tangible products auto repair car washes catering construction ... Report revenue under Wholesaling if you sell products or services to another person or business who intends to resell your product or service to a consumer.

sources.title: Seattle Shield Business & Occupation (B&O) Tax Changes
sources.issuer: City of Seattle, Office of City Finance

passages.q: Is HANGS Construction Services over the 2026 $2 million threshold?
passages.a: The B&O tax threshold will increase from $100,000 to $2 million. ... Businesses with taxable revenue of $2 million or more will be over the threshold and will be able to deduct up to $2 million of standard deduction per calendar year from their taxable revenue to arrive at their taxable amount.

checks.detail: Invoice HGC-26-0993 (Pier 9 Tech Center, $96,400.00) was coded to Bellevue, the owner's billing office, but the job site is 2200 Elliott Shore Ave W, Seattle. Seattle taxes the work where it is done, so the draft reports it in Seattle and does not deduct it as taxed by Bellevue: $96,400.00 x 0.342% = $329.69 more city tax than the register's coding. A person corrects the coding; October's change order on the same job was coded the same way. No plug posted.

checks.title: STATE-01
checks.detail: The state return is separate from this city return. The September 2026 state return reported HGC-26-0993 at location 1704 (10.30%); at the Seattle job-site rate of 10.55% the sales tax is $10,170.20 against $9,929.20 charged, $241.00 short. A person decides whether to amend that state return in My DOR and rebill the owner. This draft changes nothing on a state return. No plug posted.

checks.detail: Duwamish Gateway Logistics Center (J-2608) straddles the Seattle and Tukwila city line. All $1,994,700.00 of Q3 billings were coded to Seattle and the draft reports all of it: no deduction is claimed without evidence of where the work was done. The project manager's estimate of 60% in Seattle would take $797,880.00 out of Seattle, $2,728.75 less tax, but there is no survey or cost split, as the client's email confirms. A person obtains site evidence (the parcel survey and cost or labor hours by parcel) and decides; whether Tukwila imposes its own B&O tax decides which deduction line it would go on. No plug posted.

checks.detail: The Q3 return was due October 31, 2026 under the city's due date table, and the client's email says the date was missed. Interest also runs from the due date at the city's 2026 rate, which the page checked does not state. The city computes both when the return is filed; neither is in the draft total.
